classification.difficultyReason: Draw two specified familiar straight lines and connect their common gradient/different intercepts to the explicitly requested no-solution interpretation.

content.prompt: On the same set of axes, draw the lines $y=2x+1$ and $y=2x+3$.

answer.short: The graphs are two distinct parallel straight lines.
answer.worked: For $y=2x+1$, plot $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$. For $y=2x+3$, plot $(0,3)$ and $(-1,1)$. Draw each straight line through its two points on the same axes.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4; teacher PDF page 43, Exercise 14A question 4
spec.description: Two parallel lines on common axes, labelled with their equations and their intercepts.
spec.mathematics: Both lines have gradient 2; y-intercepts are 1 and 3 and x-intercepts are -1/2 and -3/2.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What do you notice about these two lines?

answer.short: The lines are parallel, so they will not intersect.
answer.worked: Both lines rise 2 units for every 1 unit moved to the right. They have different $y$-intercepts, so they are distinct parallel lines and never intersect.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How many solutions do the simultaneous equations have?

answer.worked: The graphs have no point of intersection, so no ordered pair satisfies both equations. There are no solutions.
